description: Single story rear extension;  alterations to roof to form hipped roof and rear dormer to the existing house; single and two story side to rear extension to create new dwelling (1 x 3 beds); front porch; replacement of existing timber boundary fence with 1.8M high brick wall; cycle / refuse storage; parking; sub division of garden ( Demolition of single story side extension and detached outbuilding)
decision_conditions: <p>The proposed location and accessibility of the refuse waste storage area is poorly located and requires opening to a public access, considered inappropriate for collection and security concern. As such, the development is contrary to Policies DM44 (Servicing) and DM45 (Waste Management) of the Harrow Local Development Management Plan (2013) and to a Policy HO2 of the draft Local Plan (2021-2041).</p>

<p>The porch and window on the proposed ground floor plan does not match with the proposed elevation drawings. Therefore, the local planning authority is unable to fully and accurately assess the proposed development. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy D3 D(7) of The London Plan (2021), Policy DM1 of the Harrow Development Management Policies Local Plan (2013) and the adopted Supplementary Planning Document: Residential Design Guide (2010).</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of the low PTAL 2 level and limited on-street parking provision would be contrary to the sustainable transport levels expected to facilitate and service conversions and redevelopment of dwellings. As such, the development is contrary to Policy DM42 (Parking standards) of the Harrow Local Development Management Plan (2013) and Policy HO2 of the draft Local Plan (2021-2041).</p>

<p>The proposed development, by reason of insufficient internal floor to ceiling height for both dwellings, would fail to support the creation of an inclusive environment in terms of daylight penetration, ventilation and cooling, and sense of space, resulting in a substandard quality of accommodation to the detriment of the residential amenities of future occupiers. As such, the development is contrary to Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy DM1 of the Harrow Local Plan (Development Management Policies) and Policy HO2 of the draft Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).</p>
